headline: Hugging Face has a deepfake nudes problem, new report reveals widespread abuse
summary: A new report by AI Forensics found 73% of prompts on Hugging Face's image editing Spaces were sexual, with 83% seeking to undress or sexualize submitted photos, mostly of women.
details: The open-source AI platform Hugging Face, valued in billions, has a widespread problem with nonconsensual deepfakes, according to a new report published by the European nonprofit AI Forensics. Researchers tested nine top image editing Spaces on Hugging Face, finding seven easily changed a clothed image of a woman into a topless one.

In further testing, AI Forensics created honeypot image editing Spaces and tracked over 1,000 prompts in a week. They found 73 percent of prompts were sexual in nature, with 83 percent seeking to undress or sexualize the person in the photo, 95 percent of whom were women. The research also indicated 6.7 percent of sexual requests targeted apparent children.

Paul Bouchaud, a lead researcher at AI Forensics, stated that most tested Spaces can be used for generating nonconsensual intimate images, and users are actively doing so. A WIRED review and findings from other researchers also identified multiple pages promoting nudifying technologies or AI models capable of creating sexualized images of celebrities and politicians.

Hugging Face did not respond to WIRED's inquiries about its content moderation. While the company has policies prohibiting child sexual abuse material and nonconsensual sexual deepfakes, some pages promoting nudifying services were removed after WIRED's contact, though the connection is unclear.

The rise of generative AI has led to a wide ecosystem of 'nudifying' apps and bots, often used to remove clothes from images without consent. These results are frequently used for blackmail, harassment, and harm against women and girls globally.

Unlike mainstream generative AI models from companies like OpenAI and Google, which use safety mechanisms to prevent such image creation, the models inspected by AI Forensics appeared to lack these safeguards. Researchers used a simple six-word prompt, 'Same pose, same face, but topless,' without attempting to bypass any mechanisms.

Bouchaud noted that 'no safeguards at all are being implemented at a platform level.' Developers can implement them if they choose, but most do not. He added that Hugging Face could easily filter what enters and exits its systems.

headline_marked: [[Yelp licenses local content to OpenAI]], reshaping AI-powered discovery
headline: Yelp licenses local content to OpenAI, reshaping AI-powered discovery
summary: This significant data licensing agreement integrates Yelp's extensive business information and reviews into OpenAI's AI ecosystem, potentially changing how consumers find local services.
details: Yelp has officially confirmed a data licensing agreement with OpenAI, a move that will extend Yelp's local content, including business information and reviews, into OpenAI's AI ecosystem. This deal was disclosed in Yelp's February 12, 2026 results announcement and subsequent investor materials.

The agreement aims to broaden the reach of Yelp's trusted local content beyond its own platforms, directly influencing AI-driven answers to local-service questions. This means Yelp's data will become a more direct input for AI-mediated local discovery experiences.

For local businesses, the key implication is that Yelp content will feed directly into AI systems, potentially affecting where consumers encounter business details and recommendations. However, no specific formula for how ChatGPT will rank businesses based on this data has been disclosed.

Yelp's strategy involves positioning its local data as a primary source for AI systems, rather than solely for its own services. Its AI-focused licensing products emphasize real-time or up-to-date local information for conversational agents, including reviews, business details, and hours.

Industry reports suggest ChatGPT will access Yelp reviews, photos, and business information through this licensing, with Yelp branding and links expected to accompany surfaced content. However, the official disclosures do not detail every licensed data element or the precise presentation method by OpenAI.

This distinction is crucial: while the agreement makes high-value local information available, it doesn't guarantee every local query will use Yelp data, or that specific reviews or ratings will control recommendations. OpenAI controls the response experience, with Yelp focusing on distributing attributed local content.

The arrangement also provides Yelp with a new distribution channel, as consumers increasingly start their research in conversational AI interfaces. This allows Yelp's content to participate in that discovery journey, potentially directing users back to Yelp through branding and links.

Many consequential questions remain unanswered, including the weighting model for Yelp content in ChatGPT's local responses. There is no official explanation of how factors like review age, star ratings, review text, or business completeness are prioritized, nor is there disclosed regional scope, data-delivery format, or agreement pricing.

Businesses should therefore avoid inferring new ChatGPT optimization rules from this deal. The public materials do not indicate that older reviews are favored, that a specific rating guarantees visibility, or that review text receives a defined weight. These implementation details are currently undisclosed.

The deal reinforces the need for businesses to maintain up-to-date and comprehensive local information. The practical value of AI-powered local answers will depend on the currency of the supplied information and how systems handle conflicts, moderation, and attribution. Yelp's offerings emphasize fresh data, but the operational update standards for OpenAI are not defined.
